_about: The sky the original pins to the camera: StaticSky, in Sky.angelscript, and on the 19
space levels SpaceSky (space_sky, below; step 122). Decoded from
android_game.bin through Enhanced's asbc listing (all_functions.txt, md5
48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0; the excerpt Step 44 read is kept at Enhanced's
out/parity/specs/lighting/work/g2/fix1/sky_functions.txt). Step 58 of
docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md.
A level places its sky where the level editor left it, and the original overwrites that
on every frame: the sky is drawn centred on the screen and one screen tall, whatever the
camera does. The port drew it where the level put it, and on 34 levels the camera moved
off it onto black (step 44's bare-ground census).
MEASURED ON THE ORIGINAL, not only read: on 16 of 16 library levels the original draws
its sky at the screen's centre to within 1 px, whatever its camera did (static_sky's
_measured).

_pixel_cover: true is THE ORIGINAL'S FRAME (planning step 145): a sky narrower than the view is drawn a
second time behind itself, out to the pixel boundaries the pixel-centre rule gives
(Sky::PixelCover), with every texel where the sky has it. Only dark_sky.png is so: it has no
fullhd twin, so it is 455 u across a view of 455.11 u at 16:9, 1279.69 px of 1280 centred,
0.16 px short of each side; the five skies with a fullhd file are 512 u wide.
The original's edge pixels, whose centres the sky covers, are the sky's: its library frames are
flat there, so no sample of an edge pixel lies in the 0.16 px strip, which a frame of one sample
a pixel at its centre gives (as would a 2x pattern at 0.25 and 0.75). Its surface is chosen by
ConfigChooser, which asks EGL for no EGL_SAMPLES and takes the first exact 5/6/5/0 match
ConfigChooser.java:24-25 and 48-66; GL2JNIView.java:121); that the first such config is
single-sampled is INFERRED from EGL 1.4's config sort (section 3.4.1.2: fewer sample buffers,
then fewer samples, first), not read on the emulator. The engine draws with 4x MSAA
(engine/src/renderer/VulkanOffscreen.cpp:15), whose samples at x 0.125 of column 0 and 0.875 of
column 1279 lie past those edges, so each edge pixel was three quarters sky and a quarter the
false draws the sky alone, as the port did before step 145.

With the cover (step 145's f420 sweep): medians 1.002 and 0.986 against the original's 1.002
and 0.988; in the rows whose inner column is the original's, the edge column is the original's

_about: ENHANCED'S OWN, not the original's (the original has no such rule; `enabled: false` draws its frame). THE SKY ON A WIDE
WINDOW. StaticSky::scaleSky sizes a sky by the screen's HEIGHT alone (skyScale = GetScreenSize().y / GetSize().y, _source
above), so the picture is 455 u of content across a view that is 256 x aspect: 455.11 u at 16:9, 554.67 at 2340 x 1080, 568.89
at 20:9, 597.33 at 21:9. Wider than 16:9 the view runs past the content and the sky ends 49.8 u (at 2340 x 1080) short of each
side; the engine's black clear colour shows there wherever the level's own art leaves an opening (a window's arch) - the tester's
black rectangle, 9.0 percent of the width. A fix is to grow the sky, about the view's centre and uniformly, until its CONTENT
covers the view with `overscan_units` to spare on each side (the quad's edge is then outside the frame's outer pixel, so
sim/EdgeCover has nothing to do there): scale = (view + 2 x overscan) / content, taller than the view by the same factor, so the
view shows the middle 1 / scale of the picture's height. Not distorted, one quad, no new entity.
`tolerance_units`: nothing happens unless the view is wider than the content by more than this. 1.0 keeps 16:9 (0.11 u over
the 455 u content: step 145's pixel cover's case) and every narrower window exactly as they were.
_content: A picture's CONTENT is its file less the black columns the artist left at each side. MEASURED, not guessed: Enhanced's
out/parity/visuals/sky/fix2/fullhd_padding.txt - sky, icy_sky, red_sky and sky_purple at fullhd are 1024 x 512 texels with black
(0, 0, 0) runs [(0, 56), (967, 1023)], so 910 texels = 455.0 u of content from 28.5 to 483.5 u. dark_sky.png (455 x 256, no
tier file), satellite_sky.png (512 x 256 u, no black columns) and every 1x file have none: a picture with no entry here is
all content. An entry is found by the file's name and the tier folder it was drawn from.

_source: Game::preLoop (Game.angelscript, bytes 112536..114414), instructions 148-182: if
Game.spaceBg, SpaceSky(); else StaticSky(sceneMax.x, 'sky', true). The controller is
added after the camera's, the portal manager's and the earthquake's (281-287), so it
reads the camera this frame left. Game.spaceBg is false by Game::Game (instruction
328) and set by Game::readProperties (116676..118260, 149-164) when the first
`properties` entity carries `space_bg` at all: CheckCustomData != 0, whatever it
holds. sceneMax.x is passed and never read.
StaticSky::StaticSky (153461..153922): GetEntityArray(name) and GetEntityArray(name +
'.ent') into m_skies - entity names 'sky' and 'sky.ent', matched exactly
(ETHBucketManager::GetEntityArrayByName, ETHBucketManager.cpp:488-503, an == on the
name) - then scaleSky(); then, handleSatellite being
true, m_satellite = SeekEntity('satellite') and, when found, its `originalPos` = its
own GetPositionXY().
StaticSky::scaleSky (154161..154942), for each sky t: skyScale = GetScreenSize().y /
GetSize().y and Scale(skyScale); m_width = GetSize().x after it; m_scrollValue =
GetFloat('scroll'); m_scroll = m_scrollValue > 0 (CMPIf 0, TP); position(t);
scrollPos = (0, 0); and for a scrolling sky SetPivotAdjust(size * (1, 0)) when t is 0
and SetPivotAdjust(size * (-1, 0)) when t is the last - `size` being the size BEFORE
the scale, and the second call replacing the first on a lone sky. The unscaled size is
what moves the picture: SetPivotAdjust stores p / GetScale() (ETHEntity.cpp:1019-1022)
and the draw subtracts pivotAdjust * scale from the position: an unrotated sky is
drawn by ETHSpriteEntity::GetScreenRect (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:742-751), less
ETHEntity::ComputeAbsoluteOrigin (ETHEntity.cpp:270-296), which adds pivotAdjust *
scale; the rotated branch (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:702-708) gives the same centre. m_width,
m_scroll and m_scrollValue are one member each, so the last sky's stand for all.
StaticSky::position (154942..155688): size = GetSize(); pitch = size * 0.5; if not
m_scroll, pitch = GetScreenSize() * 0.5; else pitch.x += size.x when t is 0 and
pitch.x -= size.x when t is the last. originalPos = pitch + (m_width * t, 0);
SetPositionXY(GetCameraPos() + originalPos + scrollPos). GetCameraPos() is the
screen's top-left corner, the video camera's position (ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:
350-356; dragon.json's camera note).
StaticSky::update (155688..156307): scrollMove = scaledUnitsPerSecond(-m_scrollValue);
for each sky position(t), then, if m_scroll, scrollPos += (scrollMove, 0) and
scrollPos = (0, 0) once abs(scrollPos.x) >= m_width. Then the satellite, when there is
one: SetPositionXY(GetCameraPos() + its originalPos).
screen_pitch is the 0.5 literal (position, instructions 18 and 32). frame_cap_ms is
STimeManager::unitsPerSecond's min(200, GetLastFrameElapsedTime())
(STimeManager.angelscript, 8045..8162), which scaledUnitsPerSecond (8284..8363)
multiplies by g_scale: a speed in the level's own units, as the port counts them.
Checked in Enhanced's out/parity/specs/ui3/work/motion/dec_state.txt: instructions 5-9
push 200, call GetLastFrameElapsedTime and min; the result is speed * that / a double
constant (read as ms to seconds) * m_factor, which STimeManager's constructor sets to 1
and pause() / resume() set to 0 / 1. The scroll branch no level reaches would therefore
also stop while the original is paused.
_units: GetScreenSize() and GetSize() are screen pixels in the original, and every entity was
multiplied by g_scale = screen.y / 256 first (SGlobalScale::scaleEntities, preLoop
instruction 37; main.angelscript's preLoop sets the 256). In the level's own units the
scale is therefore view height / picture height: 256 / 256 = 1 for every sky the levels
place, whose pictures are all 256 u tall at every tier (1x 455x256, fullhd 1024x512 at
density 2). So the port changes where a sky is drawn and not its size.
The fullhd tiers of sky, icy_sky, red_sky and sky_purple are 1024 x 512 texels whose
outer 57 columns each side are (0, 0, 0): 455 u of picture inside 512 at density 2,
with the black 28.5 u each side (Enhanced's out/parity/visuals/sky/fix2/
fullhd_padding.txt); satellite_sky is 512 u in both tiers. The 1x file is not that
picture at 1:1 on two of them (out/parity/visuals/sky/verify3/tier_geom.txt and
tier_geom2.txt): 1x sky.png is the whole fullhd image resampled to about 554 x 277 and
cropped (NCC 0.9990, against 0.8717 at 1:1), a content scale of 1.082 whose inverse,
0.924, is the visuals plan's gap D 0.9275, and 3.5 apart per pixel after a per-channel
gain and offset, a grade; red_sky is about 1.047x (NCC 0.9751 against 0.9080) and 9.4
apart after that fit; icy_sky and sky_purple are 1:1 (NCC 1.0000 and 0.9970). That
picture tier, content scale and grade, is the visuals plan's System 6, not this step's
placement. Step 66 draws it: a sky's picture is the tier file tiers.json finds, at its
units, so the four fullhd skies are 512 u wide and still scaled 1 (sim/Sprites).
_measured: Where the ORIGINAL draws its sky, on its own library frames (Enhanced's
out/parity/original/levels/<W-LL>_t8.0.png, 1280 x 720): Enhanced's
out/parity/visuals/sky/where_orig_sky.py slides the sky picture of the tier the original
draws (fullhd 512x256 u or 1x 455x256 u) over the frame and keeps the centre where the
most pixels agree. Results: out/parity/visuals/sky/where_orig_sky.txt (10 levels),
verify/where_orig_extra.txt (5 more) and fix2/where_orig_1-13.txt (1-13).
1-01 at (640, 359): 184,357 px agree there, 183,431 at the centre.
2-03 at (640, 361): 529,136 px agree there, 529,132 at the centre.
1-13 at (641, 360) at t8.0 and h6.3: 101,052 px agree there, 100,890 at the centre.
That is 16 of 16 at the screen's centre to within 1 px, including 1-01, whose level puts
its sky 2 u right and 8 u up of that, 2-01 and 4-32, whose cameras have scrolled 57 and
313 u, and 2-05 and 1-13, whose cameras have scrolled 44 and 88 u down. screen_pitch
0.5 is this.
Not scrolling, on the original's frames: the band y 0..199, x 150..599 of 3-05 and of
3-06, both scrolling_sky levels, differs by 0 at most between h2.8 and h6.3 (one run,
3.5 s apart) and between t4.5 and t8.0 (another). On 3-05 that band is all sky (100% of
it within 10 of satellite_sky pinned at the centre); on 3-06 70.3% is sky and the rest
scenery, so 3-05 is the level that shows the sky itself still.
_census: Over the 128 converted levels (tests/test_mp_sky.cpp pins it): 95 place exactly one
sky (93 named 'sky', 2 'sky.ent'), so t is 0 on every level and m_width never moves a
drawn pixel; 19 set space_bg and place `space_sky` instead; 13 place neither; one,
level14b (3-15), places a `satellite` and no sky.
NO SKY SCROLLS. No level's sky carries a `scroll` variable - not one of the 133 .esc
files and none of the sky .ent files has <Name>scroll</Name> - and GetFloat answers 0
for a missing name (ETHEntity.cpp:851-856). The `scrolling_sky` = 1 that 37 levels'
`properties` entity carries is a different variable, and the string 'scrolling_sky'
occurs nowhere in the listing's 1,473 functions, where every other properties key the
levels use is read. The original's own frames agree: in 3-05, a scrolling_sky level,
a band that is all sky (y 0..199, x 150..599) is identical to the byte in h2.8 and
h6.3, one run 3.5 s apart, and in t4.5 and t8.0 of another (3-06's same band, 70% sky,
is as still); a scroll of 1 u/s would have moved it 10 px. The scroll branch is carried
and tested as decoded; no shipped level reaches it.

_source: Game::preLoop instructions 148-182 build SpaceSky() instead of StaticSky when the first
`properties` carries `space_bg` (static_sky._source). Decoded from the listing
all_functions.txt (md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0), arguments pushed last-first
(00_order 8.0 rule 3). Planning step 122.
SpaceSky::SpaceSky (Sky.angelscript, bytes 156379..157122, listing L30669-30871):
#1-63   m_planet = SeekEntity('planet_bg.ent'), m_spiral = SeekEntity('spiral'),
m_sky = SeekEntity('space_sky'), m_eclipse = SeekEntity('eclipse.ent'): the four
*_name, each an exact == on the entity's name (ETHBucketManager.cpp:394-407), the
first in the bucket walk.
#65-99  when the spiral is there: size = GetScreenSize().length() x 1f (MULIf 1f:
spiral_diagonal_scale) and scaleToSize(m_spiral, vector2(size, size)).
scaleToSize (utilEntityEffect.angelscript, 329349..329538, L64873-64902) is
Scale(vector2(size.x / GetSize().x, size.y / GetSize().y)), and ETHEntity::Scale
MULTIPLIES the scale (ETHEntity.cpp:581-589): whatever the picture, the spiral is
drawn a square as wide as the screen's diagonal. In the level's units that is the
view's diagonal, 522.2 u at 16:9 (455.1 x 256).
#100-142 colour c = 0.7f (SetV4 1060320051: spiral_colour_default), or GetFloat('alpha')
when CheckCustomData('alpha') != 0 (spiral_colour_key; only 4-01's spiral carries
one, 0.6); SetColor(vector3(c, c, c)), which writes the rgb and keeps the alpha
(ETHEntity.cpp:493-498). The datum is named alpha and is used as a colour.
#143-199 when the planet is there: SetFloat('speed', 0.5f), SetFloat('stride', 1f), then
linearMotion(m_planet, true, 0, PI): vertical, axis 0, start angle PI
(planet_start_angle_rad: the float 3.141592654f, GameMath.h:38, registered by
ETHScriptObjRegister.cpp:512-515). That first call writes originalPos (the
level's place) and the start angle, then steps it once (motions.json).
SpaceSky::update (157259..158171, L30886-31104), every frame:
#3-13   camPos = GetCameraPos() (the screen's top-left corner), screenSize.
#15-81  the planet: SetVector3('originalPos', vector3(camPos + screenSize x
vector2(0.5, 1), its own z)) - planet_pitch - then linearMotion(m_planet, true, 0,
0) (planet_update_start_angle_rad: read only by a first call, which the
constructor has made). So the planet's entity is the bottom-centre of the view
plus (0, cos(angle) x stride x sign(speed)), angle += 0.5 x frame s a frame and
2 PI taken off once past it (linearMotion, L64429-64641).
#83-119 the sky: SetPositionXY(camPos + screenSize x V2_HALF) - sky_pitch; V2_HALF is
vector2(0.5f, 0.5f) (ETHFramework/Constants.angelscript, bytes 304963..305014,
L60203-60209). No scale: the space sky keeps its own size (512 x 256 u, hd).
#121-165 the spiral: SetPositionXY(camPos + screenSize x vector2(0.5, 1)) -
spiral_pitch, the bottom-centre - and AddToAngle(unitsPerSecond(-1.7f)):
spiral_turn_deg_per_s, Ethanon's degrees, counter-clockwise positive, so 1.7
degrees a second clockwise on the screen, capped at 200 ms a frame and still
under a pause (m_factor 0).
#167-218 the eclipse: pos = GetPosition(); SetPosition(vector3(camPos, 0) +
vector3(screenSize.x x 0.5f, pos.y, pos.z)). Its x is the view's centre
(eclipse_pitch_x); its y is its OWN y plus the camera's corner y, every frame -
it adds up. On 4-19, the one level that places it (320 u down, 64 u tall, drawn
30 u up by its pivot at scale 2), the view is the level's whole 256 u height, so
the corner's y is 0 on every frame and the eclipse holds 2 u below the view.
The planet and the eclipse keep their .ent pivots (planet_bg.ent PivotAdjust (0, 60):
the picture 60 u above its entity; eclipse.ent (0, 15) at Scale 2); the spiral's is 0,
so it turns about its centre. SpaceSky::draw is empty. ETHCallback_rocket_landing
(L96705) also moves the eclipse and brightens the spiral, but only once the game is
won (#1-3 isGameWon): that is 4-19's landing cutscene, the backlog's P2, not this.
_inferred: The constructor's linearMotion call steps the planet by the frame before the level's
first update, which no capture shows; the port steps it by one tick of the script clock
(ScriptClock::Ms(m_step), 16 ms a 60 Hz tick since planning step 147, not 1/60 s). The
most it could be is unitsPerSecond's 200 ms cap: 0.1 rad of phase, under 0.005 u of bob
near cos's floor at PI. INFERRED, not measured.
